sections.title: باب 6 — متن (10)

paras.text: … should be such that balance can be maintained. Lifting the hockey stick to the right side, hit the ball.
paras.urdu: ہونے چاہئیں تاکہ توازن برقرار رہ سکے۔ ہاکی کو دائیں جانب اٹھا کر گیند کو ہٹ کریں۔
paras.pashto: … باید داسې وي چې توازن وساتل شي. هاکي ښي لوري ته پورته کړئ او توپ ووهئ.

paras.text: By the application of Newton’s second law there is improvement in the skill. According to this law, when force is spent on a stationary ball with the help of the hockey stick, it produces acceleration in the ball in the direction of the force. The magnitude of acceleration in the ball depends on the force applied with the hockey stick; therefore the more force is spent, the farther the ball will go in the same proportion.

paras.text: Throwing the ball far while tossing it in the air is called a scoop. Along with defensive strategy, it is also sometimes used for attacking. Keeping the ball stationary, bringing the flat part of the hockey stick under the ball, bending the arms and knees, toss the ball into the air with the force of the lower hand.

paras.pashto: توپ هوا ته پورته کول او لرې غورځول سکوپ بلل کېږي؛ دا د دفاعي تګلارې تر څنګ کله کله د برید لپاره هم کارول کېږي. توپ ودروئ، د هاکي هوار برخه د توپ لاندې راوړئ، مټې او زنګونونه کاږه کړئ او د لاندېني لاس په زور توپ هوا ته پورته کړئ.

paras.text: Under projectile motion (Projectile Motion) the ball will cover distance in the air. Under the law of force, the more force applied, the farther the ball will go.
paras.urdu: بال پروجیکٹائل موشن (Projectile Motion) کے زیرِ اثر ہوا میں فاصلہ طے کرے گا۔ قوت کے قانون کے تحت جتنی قوت لگے گی بال اتنا ہی دور جائے گا۔
paras.pashto: توپ د پروجیکټایل حرکت (Projectile Motion) تر اغېز لاندې په هوا کې واټن وهي. د ځواک د قانون له مخې څومره ځواک چې ولګېږي، توپ هومره لرې ځي.

sections.theory:
… should be such that balance can be maintained. Lifting the hockey stick to the right side, hit the ball.

By the application of Newton’s second law there is improvement in the skill. According to this law, when force is spent on a stationary ball with the help of the hockey stick, it produces acceleration in the ball in the direction of the force. The magnitude of acceleration in the ball depends on the force applied with the hockey stick; therefore the more force is spent, the farther the ball will go in the same proportion.

Biomechanical principles in the scoop

Throwing the ball far while tossing it in the air is called a scoop. Along with defensive strategy, it is also sometimes used for attacking. Keeping the ball stationary, bringing the flat part of the hockey stick under the ball, bending the arms and knees, toss the ball into the air with the force of the lower hand.

Under projectile motion (Projectile Motion) the ball will cover distance in the air. Under the law of force, the more force applied, the farther the ball will go.
